body.t:

• Cascade analysis and continuous quality improvement using the data of screening activities

Drug-resistant-TB: Xpert XDR and Sequencing tests.

Four-month regimen for children 3-15 years old with non-severe pulmonary TB, 6-month (6RHZ+Eto) TB meningitis treatment regimen for children, COVID-19 vaccination for TB patients, post-TB lung disease assessment and referral
Treatment support: Nutritional support for clinically indicated clients (i.e. based on BMI/MUAC), Digital adherence technology use (Smart pillbox in addition to VOT)

Use of 6-month Bdq-Dlm-Lzd-Lfx-Cfz regimen for individuals not eligible for BPaLM regimen, especially for children, pregnant and lactating women

tables.caption: Figures 3-4. Drivers of TB in Eswatini (cases attributable to HIV, alcohol, smoking, undernutrition, diabetes) and estimated TB incidence and deaths 2010-2023
tables.content:
Figure 3 is a bar chart of the estimated number of TB cases in Eswatini attributable to five risk factors in 2023 (HIV, alcohol use disorders, smoking, undernutrition, diabetes), with uncertainty bounds; HIV is by far the largest. Figure 4 shows the estimated TB incidence rate and number of TB deaths in Eswatini, 2010-2023 (WHO Global TB Report 2024).
Key figures stated in the text: TB incidence fell from 1590/100,000 in 2010 to 335/100,000 in 2020; TB mortality in HIV-negative people fell from 56/100,000 (2010) to 24/100,000 (2020); progress was interrupted by COVID-19. HIV prevalence was 24.7% (SHIMS 3, 2021); 55% of notified cases were male in 2022.

tables.heading_path: Chapter 3: Tuberculosis Case Finding > 3.7 TB Screening Algorithms with CXR and CAD/AI Use > Figure 11: PLHIV 15+ at Facilities with X-ray and CAD/AI
tables.caption: Figure 11. TB screening algorithm for PLHIV aged 15+ at facilities with X-ray and CAD/AI: symptom screen, CXR in past 12 months, CAD result, sputum Xpert + urine LF-LAM, TPT
tables.content:
Population: PLHIV adolescents >15 years and adults (old and new) attending health facilities.
1. Symptom screen (multi-entry): current cough OR fever OR weight loss OR night sweats.
   - Positive: collect two sputum samples and 1 urine sample**; perform microbiological assessment for active TB (Xpert and LF-LAM).
   - Negative: check if CXR screening was done in the past 12 months.
     - Yes: further clinical evaluation***; provide TPT if eligible.
     - No: X-ray screen with CAD → positive: collect sputum ×2 + urine for Xpert and LF-LAM; negative: further clinical evaluation***, TPT if eligible; non-TB abnormalities*: further clinical evaluation***, TPT if eligible.
2. Microbiological result: positive → initiate TB treatment; negative → further clinical evaluation***, provide TPT if eligible.
* Abnormalities e.g. cardiomegaly, possible cancer, silicosis. ** A urine sample is collected from every client with advanced HIV disease (AHD) for LF-LAM regardless of symptoms or CAD result. *** Further clinical evaluation includes clinical assessment of resolution of TB symptoms, re-reading of the CXR by a trained clinician, and further management/specialist referral as required; if on re-reading the CXR is suggestive of TB, evaluate for TB.

Population: PLHIV (>15 years) attending ART clinics.
1. Symptom screen: current cough OR fever OR weight loss OR night sweats (WSS)*.
   - Yes: collect two sputum samples; perform Xpert for active TB diagnosis*.
   - No: is the individual on ART?

2. Xpert result: positive → initiate TB treatment; negative → further clinical evaluation, TPT if eligible.
* Perform TB-LAM for all with AHD (CD4 <200, WHO stage 3 or 4 regardless of symptoms; seriously ill regardless of CD4; all presumptive TB regardless of CD4). ** If CAD reports silicosis, refer for assessment and treatment of silicosis and provide TPT if eligible. # Abnormal (not TB): e.g. cardiomegaly, possible cancer, silicosis (if smoking history and possible cancer on CXR, highly suspicious of cancer).

tables.caption: 4.3 Microbiological diagnosis of TB and DR-TB (MTB was Detected and Rifampicin resistance not detected)

header.t: MTB was Detected and Rifampicin resistance not detected

body.t: (All patients whose diagnosis of TB has been confirmed by Xpert® MTB/RIF Ultra but without evidence of Rifampicin resistance)
Should be registered as MTBC positive, bacteriologically confirmed TB = MTB+ve/Rif-ve
Reflex Xpert MTB/XDR Assay should be done to rule out INH and fluoroquinolone resistance.
Facilities with Xpert MTB/XDR onsite are to initiate treatment after receiving Xpert MTB/XDR assay results.
Start first-line anti-TB treatment for MTB +ve/Rif -ve while waiting for Xpert MTB/XDR and DST results if not available onsite
All Xpert positive (MTB +ve/Rif-ve) cases must have reflex MGIT culture and DST done on a second sample at the time of diagnosis
Xpert MTB-positive patients should be monitored while on treatment using smear microscopy at the recommended intervals until completion of treatment.

Note: Xpert MTB/RIF® Ultra can detect dead bacilli so culture confirmation is needed for previously treated cases. Awaiting culture, should not delay initiation of TB treatment but treatment should be based on the clinical condition of the patient. If in doubt, it is also important to consult a Medical Officer.
MTB was detected, and Rifampicin resistance detected
(All patients whose diagnosis of TB has been confirmed by Xpert MTB/RIF® Ultra with evidence of Rifampicin resistance)
Should be registered as Rifampicin-resistant (RR-TB) cases = MTB +ve/Rif +ve.
RR-TB diagnosis is considered a proxy for MDR-TB; and should therefore be started on a DR-TB treatment regimen according to the DR-TB management chapter.
All Xpert diagnosed RR-TB positive (MTB +ve/Rif +ve) cases must have reflex Xpert MTB/XDR Assay to determine INH and fluoroquinolone resistance.
Targeted genome sequencing, MGIT culture and phenotypic DST should be done on the second sample at the time of diagnosis.
Xpert-diagnosed RR-TB patients should be monitored by sputum smear microscopy and MGIT culture as per the National TB management guidelines.

tables.heading_path: Chapter 4: TB and Drug-Resistant TB Diagnosis > 4.3.4 Use of LF-LAM for TB Diagnosis in PLHIV > Figure 18: Algorithm to Evaluate for TB Among PLHIV
tables.caption: Figure 18. Algorithm to evaluate for TB among PLHIV: TB symptoms/CXR/CRP, seriously ill, advanced HIV disease (AHD), urine LF-LAM and Xpert, start TB treatment, AHD package, TPT
tables.content:
Assess: TB signs and symptoms†; whether seriously ill*; advanced HIV disease (AHD)**; perform CD4 testing (if eligible); perform CXR/CRP screening if eligible and available†.
- Positive for TB symptoms and/or CXR/CRP positive for possible TB (regardless of CD4 / AHD status) → perform Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and urine LAM (if not yet done).
- AHD (regardless of TB symptoms) or seriously ill → perform urine LAM: LAM positive → perform Xpert and urine LAM (if not yet done); LAM negative → apply the AHD package of care.
- No TB symptoms, CXR/CRP negative, CD4 >200 or unknown → clinical management; provide TPT if eligible.
Results of Xpert and LAM: both negative → clinical management, provide TPT if eligible; Xpert AND/OR LAM positive → start TB treatment and perform work-up to exclude DR-TB (collect a specimen for phenotypic and genotypic DST).
† Refer to the national TB guidelines and SOP for TB screening. * Seriously ill: at least one of respiratory rate >30/min, heart rate >120/min, temperature >39°C, or unable to walk unaided. ** AHD: CD4 <200 cells or WHO clinical stage 3 or 4; for children <5 years and have not been on treatment for at least 12 months (as printed). @ CRP >5 mg/L is defined as possible/presumptive TB.
source_flags: AHD footnote for children is incomplete ('For children <5 years and have not been on treatment for at least 12 months'); WHO defines all children under 5 as having AHD, except those already stable on ART for over 12 months.
CRP threshold printed as '>5m/L' (mg/L).
'Seriously ill' uses >30/min, >120/min, >39°C here but ≥30, ≥120, ≥39°C in the Figure 16 footnote.

For AHD with a negative LAM, the chart goes straight to the AHD package without Xpert, even though LAM sensitivity is limited; clinician to confirm intent (Xpert is done if symptomatic via the first branch).

tables.heading_path: Chapter 4: TB and Drug-Resistant TB Diagnosis > Table 11: A brief details of type of EP-TB, clinical features and diagnostic procedure
tables.caption: Table 11: A brief details of type of EP-TB, clinical features and diagnostic procedure (Type of EPTB, Clinical Features, Diagnosis)

body.t:
Fever, weight loss, fatigue and occasionally night sweat or no symptoms at all.

Enlarged lymph nodes (>2cm). They can break down due to the formation of caseous pus. Cervical LN is the most common.

Mediastinal or abdominal LNs, if large may obstruct nearby 'hollow' organs producing such symptoms as stridor, dysphagia, intestinal obstruction, etc.

• Fine needle aspiration of the LN and send the specimen for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra® and Xpert MTB/XDR testing and culture/DST, and tNGS where applicable.
• If the aspirate is dry then an LN biopsy should be taken, sending the material for histological examination.

Acute or sub-acute illness varies from a few days to a few weeks.

Pleuritic chest pains, non-productive cough and dyspnoea, sometimes fever.

In an empyema complicated pleural TB, the patient may be acutely ill with chest pains, breathlessness, and cough with expectoration, fever and toxaemia. Occasionally it may be present as a chest wall mass or draining sinus tract.

• By therapeutic/diagnostic tap and sending the fluid for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra® and Xpert MTB/XDR testing and culture / DST and tNGS where applicable.
• If the patient has empyema, he must be admitted; the empyema drained and the material for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra® testing, culture/DST, and tNGS where applicable.

Meningism (neck stiffness, Kerning's sign), irritability, anorexia, vomiting, fever and sometimes seizures.

Complete or partial loss of vision is a major complication of TBM.

Without treatment the patient may descend into a coma and death would follow in five to eight weeks. Thus, patients need immediate admission.

• Lumbar puncture for CSF examination: increased lymphocytes, increased proteins and decreased glucose.
• CSF should be sent for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra®, and Xpert MTB/XDR testing and culture/DST.
• If the patient is HIV+, CSF should also be sent for CrAg and India ink staining.

Symptoms are non-specific and depend on the organs involved and extent of the disease.

Loss of appetite, malaise, diarrhea, low grade fever, weight loss, night sweats, ascites, masses or abscess, obstructive jaundice, etc.

Fever, weakness, cough, vague chest pains, dyspnoea, weight loss and swollen feet.

This is disseminated TB and patients are usually very ill with signs of systemic toxaemia: fever, circulatory collapse and tachycardia.

There may be cough, meningism and hepatosplenomegaly.

body.t: After the TB specimens have been used, all sputum cups should be kept in a bucket containing 5% hypochlorite, 10% bleach solution (freshly prepared), or 5% phenol solution. The caps of the sputum cups must be removed and the cups, caps and wooden sticks completely submerged in the solution in a secure place for at least 18 hours. After this, the solution, cups, caps and wooden sticks can be discarded with other hospital waste. This bin/bucket should have a lid which is foot operated.

Wherever incinerators exist, the type specified under the Biomedical Waste Management & Handling Rules of the country, with a combustion efficiency of 99%, should be used. Sputum cups made of polypropylene should be used wherever available. (Note: If sputum cups are made of other varieties of plastic, they should be disinfected and destroyed as per the hospital waste management rules). Burning is NOT recommended.

The sputum cups and lids, with the lids removed, along with wooden sticks can be autoclaved at the end of each day's laboratory work. The autoclave cycle should have a holding time of 15 minutes at 121°C HTAT (Holding time at temperature), 10 minutes at 126°C HTAT or 3 minutes at 134°C HTAT. The material can be discarded with other waste after proper cooling.

body.t:
• Can be performed at any age
• Collection of sputa after the child inhales 3-5% hypertonic saline (induction improves the yield of sputa collection for all ages)
• The child should not have eaten for 2 hours before the procedure and pretreated with salbutamol
• Nasopharyngeal suctioning can be performed following the procedure if the child is unable to expectorate
• Can be performed at any time but morning is preferred
• 5 ml is recommended for Gene Xpert and Culture
• Do not perform in children with respiratory distress or wheeze
• A nebulizer and mask must be sterilized after each use

• Consider in children < 7 years
• Nasogastric aspiration of gastric secretions using a nasogastric tube
• 2-3 specimens are recommended to increase yield
• Volume: 5-10 ml should be collected, if less confirm tube placement and re-attempt. If still < 5-10 ml instill up to 20 ml of sterile water and re-aspirate.
• It should be performed in the early morning and fast for 4 hours (outpatient collection is fine provided these parameters are met).
• Nasogastric tube should be used
• If possible, neutralize the aspirate with sodium bicarbonate if the specimen is not processed that day based on pH testing

• Can be performed in children under 6 years
• Suctioning of the nasopharynx via a nasopharyngeal tube at 15 -20 kPa of pressure
• 2 ml of aspirate is recommended
• Can be performed at any time but morning is preferred, generally follows sputum induction
• A suction machine is recommended for the procedure

• Performed only for children under the age of 15 years.
• For infants and toddlers, stools can be directly collected from the diaper as soon as possible after defecation. (Avoiding prolonged contact with the surface of the diaper.)
• Older children are directed to defecate on a clean sheet of paper, avoiding contamination from the soil and urine.
• Using a designated spatula or wooden stick, the sample is transferred into a stool container or a sputum container and sealed tightly before submitting it to the laboratory for processing. The sample container should NOT be filled to the brim.
• A volume of 1g (a pea size) for a formed stool or 5 ml for a watery stool is sufficient to perform the Xpert test.
• The simple one-step method (SOS) is used in the laboratory to analyse the sample.
• A subsequently induced sputum or gastric aspirate will have to be collected and sent for culture and DST to the reference lab should the Xpert MTB results turn out positive.
Methods of specimen collection for Extra-Pulmonary Disease
• Specimen collection should be attempted from the presumed site of disease through fine needle aspiration of lymph nodes, collection of CSFS, pleural, ascetic fluid etc.

Population: children and adolescents <15 years attending health facilities.
1. Symptom screen: for 10–15 years, current cough OR fever OR weight loss OR night sweats (W4SS); for <10 years, cough, fever, weight loss/poor weight gain of any duration, or history of TB contact.
   - Positive: collect two specimens (if <5 years or cannot produce sputum, collect one stool sample) and perform microbiological assessment for active TB (including LF-LAM for children living with HIV*).

No: CXR read by a human reader → suggestive of TB: collect specimens as above; negative: further clinical evaluation, TPT if eligible; non-TB abnormalities: clinical assessment for active TB if symptoms persist or other morbidity, take CXR if not taken before, provide TPT if eligible.
2. Microbiological result: positive → initiate TB treatment; negative → clinical assessment for active TB if symptoms persist or other morbidity, take CXR if not taken before, provide TPT if eligible.

tables.heading_path: Chapter 9: Pharmacovigilance and Adverse Event Management > 9.9 Algorithms for Management of Adverse Events with Second-line Anti-TB Drugs > Figure 28: Management of QTc Prolongation
tables.caption: Figure 28. Management of QTcF prolongation on second-line TB drugs (BDQ, CFZ, MFX, DLM, LFX): ECG monitoring, grades 1-4 and actions, order of stopping drugs
tables.content:
Items: If on multiple QtcF prolonging drugs, stop ancillary drugs first. Then stop MFX if receiving this drug. If QTcF prolongation persists, then stop CFZ. If CTcF prolongation persists, then stop BDQ.
- Causative Medications: BDQ, CFZ, MFX, DLM, LFX -> QTcF prolongation: Signs and symptoms include palpitations, syncope/fainting, dizziness
- Monitor for QTcF prolongation by checking an ECG at baseline, week 2 and monthly until month 6 or anytime if there are symptoms -> QTcF prolongation: Signs and symptoms include palpitations, syncope/fainting, dizziness
- QTcF prolongation: Signs and symptoms include palpitations, syncope/fainting, dizziness -> Assess ECG. If QtcF is prolonged, repeat ECG. Consider other possible causes including low potassium, malnutrition, hypothyroidism or other medications. Consider checking and replacing potassium if vomiting or diarrhea.
- Assess ECG. If QtcF is prolonged, repeat ECG. Consider other possible causes including low potassium, malnutrition, hypothyroidism or other medications. Consider checking and replacing potassium if vomiting or diarrhea. -> Assess severity and manage
- Assess severity and manage -> Mild/Grade 1: *45 - 480 msec* Monitor closely, weekly ECG until QTcF < grade or baseline; correct electrolytes or other causes as needed; Moderate/Grade 2: *> 480 - 500 msec* Monitor closely, weekly ECG until QTcF < grade or baseline; correct electrolytes or other causes as needed; Severe/Grade 3: *> 500 msec* Stop the suspected causative drug(s); hospitalize and correct electrolytes or other underlying causes as needed; Life-threatening/Grade 4: *> 501 msec or 60 msec change from baseline and one of the following:* Torsades de pointers polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, or signs/symptoms or serious arrhythmia. Stop the suspected causative drugs; hospitalize and correct electrolytes or other underlying causes
source_flags: Grade 1 is printed as '45 - 480 msec' (presumably 451-480 msec); grade 4 as '> 501 msec or 60 msec change' (usually >500 msec or >60 msec increase from baseline).
'CTcF' typo in the drug-stopping note.

tables.heading_path: Chapter 9: Pharmacovigilance and Adverse Event Management > 9.9 Algorithms for Management of Adverse Events with Second-line Anti-TB Drugs > Figure 31: Management of Liver Function Abnormalities
tables.caption: Figure 31. Management of liver function abnormalities on TB drugs (PZA, INH, BDQ, CFZ, Eto, PAS): LFT monitoring, grades 1-4 by ULN, stop and reintroduce drugs, liver-sparing regimen
tables.content:
- Causative Medications: PZA, INH, BDQ, CFZ, Eto, PAS -> Liver Function Abnormalities: Liver function test abnormalities can present asymptomaticaly or with abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, jaundice/icterus, itching
- Monitor elevated liver function tests at baseline and monthly for the first six months of treatment and anytime if there are symptoms -> Liver Function Abnormalities: Liver function test abnormalities can present asymptomaticaly or with abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, jaundice/icterus, itching
- Liver Function Abnormalities: Liver function test abnormalities can present asymptomaticaly or with abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, jaundice/icterus, itching -> Assess for other causes. These include alcohol use, use of traditional medicines/ herbs, viral hepatitis and TB itself
- Assess for other causes. These include alcohol use, use of traditional medicines/ herbs, viral hepatitis and TB itself -> Assess severity and manage
- Assess severity and manage -> Mild/Grade 1: >1 to 2.5 times ULN and asymptomatic Continue treatment and follow until return to baseline or stabilization of AST/ALT elevation; Moderate/Grade 2: >2.5 to 5 times ULN and asymptomatic Continue treatment and follow until return to baseline or stabilization of AST/ALT elevation; Severe/Grade 3: > 5 to 10 ULN or any asymptomatic elevations Stop all drugs, measure LFTs weekly; reintroduce drugs after toxicity is resolved; Life-threatening/Grade 4: > 10 time ULN regardless of symptoms Stop all drugs, measure LFTs weekly; reintroduce drugs after toxicity is resolved
Liver-sparing regimen drugs: EMB, DLM, CS, amikacin (with caution) and likely the FQs. People with underlying liver disease, heavy alcohol use or viral hepatitis should start a modified shorter regimen that includes CS and does NOT include INH or PZA.
source_flags: Grade 3 reads '> 5 to 10 ULN or any asymptomatic elevations' – probably 'symptomatic' (drug-induced liver injury is usually ALT >3×ULN with symptoms or >5×ULN without).

tables.heading_path: Chapter 9: Pharmacovigilance and Adverse Event Management > 9.9 Algorithms for Management of Adverse Events with Second-line Anti-TB Drugs > Figure 32: Management of Anaemia/ Thrombocytopenia
tables.caption: Figure 32: Management of Anaemia/ Thrombocytopenia (linezolid, AZT, CTX): severity grades and linezolid action
tables.content:
- Causative Medications: LZD, AZT, CTX -> Anaemia / Thrombocytopenia
- Monitor elevated Anaemia / Thrombocytopenia checking baseline and monthly FBC and anytime if there are symptoms -> Anaemia / Thrombocytopenia
- Anaemia / Thrombocytopenia: Anaemia: Signs and symptoms include bruising, pallor, SOB, Fatigue, palpitations, dizziness. Thrombocytopenia: Easy bruising, bleeding tendencies -> Assess for other causes
- Assess for other causes. For anaemia, there multiple other causes, including TB itself, HIV, malignancy, iron deficiency, alcohol use, pregnancy, bleeding. For thrombocytopenia, some viruses may lead to prolonged or excessive bleeding -> Assess severity and manage
- Assess severity and manage -> Mild/Grade 1: Hb: 9.5 - 10.5g/dl; Plt: 75,000 - 99,000/mm3. Continue linezolid. Monitor closely; 2 weekly FBC (If HB continues to decline reduce to 300 mg)
- Assess severity and manage -> Moderate/Grade 2: Hb: 8.0 - 9.4g/dl; Plt: 50,000 - 74,999mm3. Reduce linezolid dose to 300 mg. 2 weekly FBC. Monitor closely
- Assess severity and manage -> Severe/Grade 3: HB: 6.5-7.9g/dl; Plt: 20,000 - 49,999/mm3. Stop linezolid. Consider transfusion. Weekly FBC. Reinitiate 300mg/day if myelosuppression recovers within first 2 months of treatment
- Assess severity and manage -> Life-threatening/Grade 4: Hb: < 6.5g/dl; Plt: < 20,000. Stop linezolid. Consider transfusion. Weekly FBC. Reinitiate 300mg/day if myelosuppression recovers within first 2 months of treatment
Note (box below the chart): Patient with baseline anaemia of all grades can be treated with LZD. They should have more frequent FBC monitoring (i.e. every 2 weeks). This is true even of patients with Grade 3 or Grade 4 anemia, provided they are started on therapy as inpatients and that they have weekly FBC checked.

Developing DS-TB while on a protease inhibitor (PI)-based ART regimen

Consult an experienced HIV clinician or snapthirdline@mohcoag.org before choosing these options:
TB patient on LPV/r:
- Super-boost LPV/r to 400 mg/400 mg by adding 300 mg ritonavir, and continue until 2 weeks after completion of TB treatment

tables.caption: Table 62: Management of TPT interruption or missed dose

body.t: If the missed dose is remembered within the next 2 days, continue to take the remaining doses according to the original schedule. If the missed dose is remembered > 2 days later, take the missed dose immediately, and change the schedule for weekly intake to the day the missed dose was taken, until treatment completion. This will avoid 2 weekly doses being taken fewer than 4 days apart.

If treatment interruption occurred after at least 9 doses were taken within 12 weeks of starting, continue and complete the remaining doses, thus prolonging the total treatment duration to a maximum of 112 days. If ≥ 4 weekly doses are missed, consider restarting the full TPT course. If an individual has difficulty adhering to a weekly routine, consider dis continuing 3HP and offering an alternative regimen with daily dosing.
Continue and complete the remaining doses, thus prolonging the total treatment duration to a maximum of 6 weeks (42 days from starting TPT)

If < 7 consecutive doses were missed, consider restarting the complete course of the 1HP regimen. If > 7 doses were missed intermittently, continue and complete the remaining doses, thus prolonging the total treatment duration to a maximum of 6 weeks (42 days from starting TPT)

Resume TPT and add the number of missed doses to the total treatment duration.
Do not change the scheduled date of the next follow-up visit, but postpone the last follow-up visit by the number of extra days to compensate for missed doses. For example, if a child on 3HR misses 3 days of treatment, continue TPT for a total of 3 months + 3 days from the date of start.

If treatment interruption occurs after more than 80% of doses in the regimen have been taken, continue and complete the remaining treatment as per the original plan. If less than 80% of doses in the regimen were taken, and the treatment course can still be completed within the expected treatment duration + 33% additional time, continue and complete the remaining treatment as per the original plan. For example, if an adult on 6H had taken only 120 doses by month 6, the remaining 62 doses can be taken in the next 2 months, without exceeding the 239-day limit. If < 80% of doses in the regimen were taken, and the treatment course cannot be completed within the expected time, consider restarting the full TPT course. A shorter regimen would be preferable.
